sanskrit: māṃ praviśya bhavantīha muktā bhaktās tu ye mama ahaṃ hi puruṣo jñeyo niṣkriyaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ
english: Those devotees of mine who are liberated enter into me and abide here. For I am to be known as the Puruṣa, actionless, the twenty-fifth principle.

sanskrit: nirguṇo niṣkalaś caiva nirdvaṃdvo niṣparigrahaḥ etat tvayā na vijñeyaṃ rūpavān iti dṛśyate icchan muhūrtān naśyeyam īśo 'haṃ jagato guruḥ
english: Devoid of qualities, without parts, free from the pairs of opposites, without possessions am I. This you cannot fully grasp — though I am seen to possess a form. Should I so wish, I could vanish in an instant, for I am the Lord, the teacher of the world.

sanskrit: māyā hy eṣā mayā sṛṣṭā yan māṃ paśyasi nārada sarvabhūtaguṇair yuktaṃ naivaṃ tvaṃ jñātum arhasi mayaitat kathitaṃ samyak tava mūrticatuṣṭayam
english: For this is māyā, fashioned by me, that you behold me, O Nārada, as endowed with the qualities of all beings; thus you ought not to know me. By me has been rightly told to you my fourfold manifestation.

sanskrit: siddhā hy ete mahābhāgā narā hy ekāntino 'bhavan tamorajobhyāṃ nirmuktāḥ pravekṣyanti ca māṃ mune
english: For these greatly blessed men have become perfected, single-minded ones; freed from darkness and passion they shall enter into me, O sage.

sanskrit: ahaṃ kartā ca kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ cāpi nārada ahaṃ hi jīvasaṃjño vai mayi jīvaḥ samāhitaḥ maivaṃ te buddhir atrābhūd dṛṣṭo jīvo mayeti ca
english: I am the doer, the deed, and the cause as well, O Nārada; I indeed am that which bears the name of the living soul, and in me the living soul is gathered up. Let not this thought arise in you here: 'the living soul has been seen by me.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ sarvatrago brahman bhūtagrāmāntarātmakaḥ bhūtagrāmaśarīreṣu naśyatsu na naśāmy aham
english: I am all-pervading, O brahmin, the inner self of the host of beings; though the bodies in the host of beings perish, I do not perish.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbho lokādiś caturvaktro niruktagaḥ brahmā sanātano devo mama bahvarthacintakaḥ
english: Hiraṇyagarbha, the origin of the worlds, the four-faced one, versed in etymology, Brahmā the eternal god, is the ponderer of my manifold purposes.

sanskrit: paśyaikādaśa me rudrān dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvam āsthitān dvādaśaiva tathādityān vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ samāsthitān
english: Behold my eleven Rudras stationed at my right side, and likewise the twelve Ādityas standing together at my left.

sanskrit: agrataś caiva me paśya vasūn aṣṭau surottamān nāsatyaṃ caiva dasraṃ ca bhiṣajau paśya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: And before me behold the eight Vasus, foremost of the gods; and behind me behold the two physicians, Nāsatya and Dasra.

sanskrit: sarvān prajāpatīn paśya paśya sapta ṛṣīn api vedān yajñāṃś ca śataśaḥ paśyāmṛtam athauṣadhīḥ
english: Behold all the Prajāpatis, behold too the seven seers, the Vedas, and the sacrifices by the hundreds; behold the nectar of immortality and the healing herbs.

sanskrit: tapāṃsi niyamāṃś caiva yamān api pṛthagvidhān tathāṣṭaguṇam aiśvaryam ekasthaṃ paśya mūrtimat
english: Behold the austerities and the observances, and the restraints of various kinds, and the eightfold lordly power gathered in one place, embodied in form.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ lakṣmīṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca kakudminīm vedānāṃ mātaraṃ paśya matsthāṃ devīṃ sarasvatīm
english: Behold Śrī, and Lakṣmī, and Kīrti, and the Earth bearing her summits, and the goddess Sarasvatī, mother of the Vedas, abiding in me.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ ca jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ paśya nārada khecaram ambhodharān samudrāṃś ca sarāṃsi saritas tathā
english: And behold Dhruva, best of the heavenly lights, the sky-traveler, O Nārada; the rain-bearing clouds, the oceans, the lakes, and the rivers as well.

sanskrit: mūrtimantaḥ pitṛgaṇāṃś caturaḥ paśya sattama trīṃś caivemān guṇān paśya matsthān mūrtivivarjitān
english: Behold the four hosts of the fathers in embodied form, O most excellent one; and behold these three qualities, abiding in me yet devoid of form.

sanskrit: devakāryād api mune pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate devānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca pitā hy eko 'ham āditaḥ
english: More distinguished even than rites for the gods, O sage, is the rite for the fathers; for of both the gods and the fathers I alone am the one father from the beginning.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hayaśiro bhūtvā samudre paścimottare pibāmi suhutaṃ havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca śraddhayānvitam
english: Becoming Hayaśiras, the horse-headed one, in the northwestern ocean, I drink the well-offered oblation and the offering to the fathers, both attended with faith.

sanskrit: mayā sṛṣṭaḥ purā brahmā madyajñam ayajat svayam tatas tasmai varān prīto dadāv aham anuttamān
english: Of old Brahmā was created by me, and he himself offered sacrifice to me; then, well pleased, I granted him boons beyond compare.

sanskrit: matputratvaṃ ca kalpādau lokādhyakṣatvam eva ca ahaṃkārakṛtaṃ caiva nāma paryāyavācakam
english: Sonship to me at the dawn of each aeon, and overlordship of the worlds, and a name born of self-consciousness that designates him by his synonyms.

sanskrit: tvayā kṛtāṃ ca maryādāṃ nātikrāmyati kaś cana tvaṃ caiva varado brahman varepsūnāṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: 'No one shall transgress the boundary that you have set, and you yourself, O brahmin, shall be the bestower of boons to those who desire boons.'

sanskrit: surāsuragaṇānāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tapodhana pitṝṇāṃ ca mahābhāga satataṃ saṃśitavrata vividhānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ tvam upāsyo bhaviṣyasi
english: 'Of the hosts of gods and demons, and of the seers, O wealthy in austerity, and of the fathers, O greatly blessed one of rigorously kept vows, and of the manifold beings, you shall ever be the worshipful one.'

sanskrit: prādurbhāvagataś cāhaṃ surakāryeṣu nityadā anuśāsyas tvayā brahman niyojyaś ca suto yathā
english: 'And I, having come into manifestation in the affairs of the gods, am ever to be instructed by you, O brahmin, and to be set to my task, as a son is.'

sanskrit: etāṃś cānyāṃś ca rucirān brahmaṇe 'mitatejase ahaṃ dattvā varān prīto nivṛttiparamo 'bhavam
english: Having granted these and other splendid boons to Brahmā of measureless splendor, I, well pleased, became wholly devoted to withdrawal.

sanskrit: nirvāṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nivṛttiḥ paramā smṛtā tasmān nivṛttim āpannaś caret sarvāṅganirvṛtaḥ
english: The extinction of all duties — withdrawal — is remembered as the supreme state; therefore, having attained withdrawal, let one move through the world with every faculty at rest.

sanskrit: vidyāsahāyavantaṃ mām ādityasthaṃ sanātanam kapilaṃ prāhur ācāryāḥ sāṃkhyaniścitaniścayāḥ
english: Me, accompanied by knowledge, abiding in the sun, the eternal one, the teachers whose convictions are settled by Sāṃkhya call Kapila.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān eṣa chandasi suṣṭutaḥ so 'haṃ yogagatir brahman yogaśāstreṣu śabditaḥ
english: This blessed Hiraṇyagarbha, well praised in the Vedic hymns — that am I, named in the Yoga treatises as the goal of yoga, O brahmin.

sanskrit: eṣo 'haṃ vyaktim āgamya tiṣṭhāmi divi śāśvataḥ tato yugasahasrānte saṃhariṣye jagat punaḥ kṛtvātmasthāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: Having come into manifestation, I abide everlasting in heaven; then, at the end of a thousand ages, I shall withdraw the world again, having drawn into myself the beings, both the unmoving and the moving.

sanskrit: ekākī vidyayā sārdhaṃ vihariṣye dvijottama tato bhūyo jagat sarvaṃ kariṣyāmīha vidyayā
english: Alone, together with knowledge, I shall sport, O best of the twice-born; then once more I shall fashion the whole world here through knowledge.

sanskrit: asmanmūrtiś caturthī yā sāsṛjac cheṣam avyayam sa hi saṃkarṣaṇaḥ proktaḥ pradyumnaṃ so 'py ajījanat
english: That fourth form of mine created the imperishable Śeṣa; he indeed is called Saṃkarṣaṇa, and he too begot Pradyumna.

sanskrit: pradyumnād aniruddho 'haṃ sargo mama punaḥ punaḥ aniruddhāt tathā brahmā tatrādikamalodbhavaḥ
english: From Pradyumna I am Aniruddha — my creation recurs again and again; and from Aniruddha comes Brahmā, born from the primal lotus there.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaḥ sarvabhūtāni carāṇi sthāvarāṇi ca etāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ vijānīhi kalpādiṣu punaḥ punaḥ
english: From Brahmā arise all beings, both the moving and the unmoving. Know this to be the creation that recurs again and again at the dawn of each aeon.

sanskrit: yathā sūryasya gaganād udayāstamayāv iha naṣṭau punar balāt kāla ānayaty amitadyutiḥ tathā balād ahaṃ pṛthvīṃ sarvabhūtahitāya vai
english: As Time of measureless brilliance forcibly brings back again the sun's rising and setting once they have vanished from the sky here, so by my power do I, for the welfare of all beings, restore the Earth —

sanskrit: sattvair ākrāntasarvāṅgāṃ naṣṭāṃ sāgaramekhalām ānayiṣyāmi svaṃ sthānaṃ vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ
english: — her whole body overrun by creatures, sunk away, girded by the ocean, I shall bring back to her own place, having taken on the boar's form.

sanskrit: hiraṇyākṣaṃ haniṣyāmi daiteyaṃ balagarvitam nārasiṃhaṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā hiraṇyakaśipuṃ punaḥ surakārye haniṣyāmi yajñaghnaṃ ditinandanam
english: I shall slay Hiraṇyākṣa, the son of Diti, drunk with his strength; and again, taking on the man-lion form, for the gods' sake I shall slay Hiraṇyakaśipu, that destroyer of sacrifice, the son of Diti.

sanskrit: virocanasya balavān baliḥ putro mahāsuraḥ bhaviṣyati sa śakraṃ ca svarājyāc cyāvayiṣyati
english: Bali, the mighty son of Virocana, a great demon, shall come to be, and he shall cast Śakra down from his own sovereignty.

sanskrit: trailokye 'pahṛte tena vimukhe ca śacīpatau adityāṃ dvādaśaḥ putraḥ saṃbhaviṣyāmi kaśyapāt
english: When the three worlds have been carried off by him, and the lord of Śacī is turned away helpless, I shall be born as the twelfth son in Aditi, from Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: tato rājyaṃ pradāsyāmi śakrāyāmitatejase devatāḥ sthāpayiṣyāmi sveṣu sthāneṣu nārada baliṃ caiva kariṣyāmi pātālatalavāsinam
english: Then I shall restore the kingdom to Śakra of measureless splendor; I shall establish the gods in their own stations, O Nārada, and Bali I shall make a dweller in the depths of the netherworld.

sanskrit: tretāyuge bhaviṣyāmi rāmo bhṛgukulodvahaḥ kṣatraṃ cotsādayiṣyāmi samṛddhabalavāhanam
english: In the Tretā age I shall become Rāma, upholder of the lineage of Bhṛgu, and I shall root out the warrior order, abounding in forces and mounts.

sanskrit: saṃdhau tu samanuprāpte tretāyāṃ dvāparasya ca rāmo dāśarathir bhūtvā bhaviṣyāmi jagatpatiḥ
english: And when the juncture of the Tretā and the Dvāpara has arrived, becoming Rāma the son of Daśaratha, I shall be the lord of the world.

sanskrit: tritopaghātād vairūpyam ekato 'tha dvitas tathā prāpsyato vānaratvaṃ hi prajāpatisutāv ṛṣī
english: Through harm done to Trita, the two seers, sons of Prajāpati — Ekata and likewise Dvita — incurring disfigurement, shall attain the condition of monkeys.

sanskrit: tayor ye tv anvaye jātā bhaviṣyanti vanaukasaḥ te sahāyā bhaviṣyanti surakārye mama dvija
english: Those forest-dwellers who shall be born in their line shall become my helpers in the gods' undertaking, O twice-born.

sanskrit: tato rakṣaḥpatiṃ ghoraṃ pulastyakulapāṃsanam haniṣye rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye sagaṇaṃ lokakaṇṭakam
english: Then in battle I shall slay the terrible lord of the rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, the defiler of Pulastya's line, that thorn in the world's side, together with his host.

sanskrit: dvāparasya kaleś caiva saṃdhau paryavasānike prādurbhāvaḥ kaṃsahetor mathurāyāṃ bhaviṣyati
english: At the final juncture of the Dvāpara and the Kali ages, my manifestation, for the sake of Kaṃsa, shall come to be in Mathurā.

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ dānavān hatvā subahūn devakaṇṭakān kuśasthalīṃ kariṣyāmi nivāsaṃ dvārakāṃ purīm
english: There, having slain very many dānavas, those thorns in the gods' side, I shall make Kuśasthalī, the city of Dvārakā, my dwelling.

sanskrit: vasānas tatra vai puryām aditer vipriyaṃkaram haniṣye narakaṃ bhaumaṃ muraṃ pīṭhaṃ ca dānavam
english: Dwelling there in that city, I shall slay Naraka the son of the Earth, doer of displeasure to Aditi, and Mura, and the dānava Pīṭha.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣapuraṃ ramyaṃ nānādhanasamanvitam kuśasthalīṃ nayiṣyāmi hatvā vai dānavottamān
english: The lovely city of Prāgjyotiṣa, filled with manifold treasures, I shall carry off to Kuśasthalī, having slain the foremost of the dānavas.

sanskrit: śaṃkaraṃ ca mahāsenaṃ bāṇapriyahitaiṣiṇam parājeṣyāmy athodyuktau devalokanamaskṛtau
english: And Śaṃkara and Mahāsena, who seek the welfare and pleasure of Bāṇa, both girded for the fight and honored by the world of the gods — these I shall vanquish.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutaṃ baler jitvā bāṇaṃ bāhusahasriṇam vināśayiṣyāmi tataḥ sarvān saubhanivāsinaḥ
english: Then, having conquered Bali's son Bāṇa of the thousand arms, I shall destroy thereafter all the dwellers in Saubha.

sanskrit: yaḥ kālayavanaḥ khyāto gargatejobhisaṃvṛtaḥ bhaviṣyati vadhas tasya matta eva dvijottama
english: He who shall be known as Kālayavana, enveloped in the splendor of Garga — his slaying shall come from me alone, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhaś ca balavān sarvarājavirodhakaḥ bhaviṣyaty asuraḥ sphīto bhūmipālo girivraje mama buddhiparispandād vadhas tasya bhaviṣyati
english: And the mighty Jarāsaṃdha, opposer of all kings, shall come to be a swollen demon, a ruler of the earth in Girivraja; his slaying shall come about through the working of my design.

sanskrit: samāgateṣu baliṣu pṛthivyāṃ sarvarājasu vāsaviḥ susahāyo vai mama hy eko bhaviṣyati
english: When the powerful ones, all the kings upon the earth, are gathered together, the son of Vāsava alone shall be my good helper.

sanskrit: evaṃ lokā vadiṣyanti naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī udyuktau dahataḥ kṣatraṃ lokakāryārtham īśvarau
english: Thus the worlds shall say: 'The two seers Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the two lords, girded for the work, are consuming the warrior order for the sake of the world's purpose.'

sanskrit: kṛtvā bhārāvataraṇaṃ vasudhāyā yathepsitam sarvasātvatamukhyānāṃ dvārakāyāś ca sattama kariṣye pralayaṃ ghoram ātmajñātivināśanam
english: Having relieved the Earth of her burden as I desired, O most excellent one, I shall bring about a terrible dissolution of all the chief Sātvatas and of Dvārakā, destroying my own kinsmen.

sanskrit: karmāṇy aparimeyāni caturmūrtidharo hy aham kṛtvā lokān gamiṣyāmi svān ahaṃ brahmasatkṛtān
english: For I, bearer of the fourfold form, having performed deeds beyond all measure, shall go to my own worlds, honored by Brahman.

sanskrit: haṃso hayaśirāś caiva prādurbhāvā dvijottama yadā vedaśrutir naṣṭā mayā pratyāhṛtā tadā savedāḥ saśrutīkāś ca kṛtāḥ pūrvaṃ kṛte yuge
english: The Swan and the Horse-headed one too were manifestations, O best of the twice-born; when the sacred utterance of the Veda was lost, then it was recovered by me — and with their Vedas and revealed texts restored, men were set aright of old in the Kṛta age.

sanskrit: atikrāntāḥ purāṇeṣu śrutās te yadi vā kva cit atikrāntāś ca bahavaḥ prādurbhāvā mamottamāḥ lokakāryāṇi kṛtvā ca punaḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ gatāḥ
english: These have passed away in ages gone by, whether heard of in the ancient lore or somewhere else; and many of my surpassing manifestations have passed away, having done the works of the world and then returned to their own essential nature.

sanskrit: na hy etad brahmaṇā prāptam īdṛśaṃ mama darśanam yat tvayā prāptam adyeha ekāntagatabuddhinā
english: For not even by Brahmā has such a vision of me been gained as you have gained today here, your mind set upon the single-pointed path.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ brahman bhaktimato mayā purāṇaṃ ca bhaviṣyaṃ ca sarahasyaṃ ca sattama
english: All this has been declared to you, O brahmin, devoted as you are, by me — the past and the future, together with its secret, O most excellent one.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavān devo viśvamūrtidharo 'vyayaḥ etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Thus that blessed god, bearer of the universal form, the imperishable one, having spoken just so much speech, vanished there and then.

sanskrit: nārado 'pi mahātejāḥ prāpyānugraham īpsitam naranārāyaṇau draṣṭuṃ prādravad badarāśramam
english: And Nārada of great splendor, having received the grace he longed for, hastened to the hermitage of Badarī to behold Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: idaṃ mahopaniṣadaṃ caturvedasamanvitam sāṃkhyayogakṛtaṃ tena pañcarātrānuśabditam
english: This great Upaniṣad, conjoined with the four Vedas, wrought of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, named in keeping with the Pañcarātra —

sanskrit: nārāyaṇamukhodgītaṃ nārado 'śrāvayat punaḥ brahmaṇaḥ sadane tāta yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathā śrutam
english: — sung forth from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa, Nārada recited again in the abode of Brahmā, my son, just as he had seen and just as he had heard.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca etad āścaryabhūtaṃ hi māhātmyaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ kiṃ brahmā na vijānīte yataḥ śuśrāva nāradāt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Wondrous indeed is the greatness of that wise one; does Brahmā not know it, that he had to hear of it from Nārada?

sanskrit: pitāmaho hi bhagavāṃs tasmād devād anantaraḥ kathaṃ sa na vijānīyāt prabhāvam amitaujasaḥ
english: For the blessed Grandsire stands next after that god; how should he not know the power of him whose might is measureless?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mahākalpasahasrāṇi mahākalpaśatāni ca samatītāni rājendra sargāś ca pralayāś ca ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Thousands of great aeons and hundreds of great aeons have passed away, O lord of kings, and creations too, and dissolutions.

sanskrit: sargasyādau smṛto brahmā prajāsargakaraḥ prabhuḥ jānāti devapravaraṃ bhūyaś cāto 'dhikaṃ nṛpa paramātmānam īśānam ātmanaḥ prabhavaṃ tathā
english: At the dawn of creation Brahmā is remembered as the lord, maker of the bringing forth of creatures; he knows the foremost of gods, and beyond that yet more, O king — the Supreme Self, the ruler, and the source of his own being.

sanskrit: ye tv anye brahmasadane siddhasaṃghāḥ samāgatāḥ tebhyas tac chrāvayām āsa purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam
english: And to those other gathered companies of the perfected ones in Brahmā's abode, he made heard that ancient lore, equal in authority to the Veda.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sakāśāt sūryaś ca śrutvā vai bhāvitātmanām ātmānugāmināṃ brahma śrāvayām āsa bhārata
english: And the Sun, having heard it from those purified souls who follow the Self, made the sacred teaching heard, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ṣaṭṣaṣṭir hi sahasrāṇi ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām sūryasya tapato lokān nirmitā ye puraḥsarāḥ teṣām akathayat sūryaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: For sixty-six thousand seers of purified souls, who were created as the forerunners of the Sun as he warmed the worlds — to all those purified souls the Sun recounted it.

sanskrit: sūryānugāmibhis tāta ṛṣibhis tair mahātmabhiḥ merau samāgatā devāḥ śrāvitāś cedam uttamam
english: By those great-souled seers who follow the Sun, my son, the gods gathered upon Meru were made to hear this supreme teaching.

sanskrit: devānāṃ tu sakāśād vai tataḥ śrutvāsito dvijaḥ śrāvayām āsa rājendra pitṝṇāṃ munisattamaḥ
english: And the brahmin Asita, having then heard it from the gods, made it heard to the fathers, that best of sages, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: mama cāpi pitā tāta kathayām āsa śaṃtanuḥ tato mayaitac chrutvā ca kīrtitaṃ tava bhārata
english: And my father too, Śaṃtanu, my son, recounted it; thus, having heard it, I have related it to you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: surair vā munibhir vāpi purāṇaṃ yair idaṃ śrutam sarve te paramātmānaṃ pūjayanti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Whether gods or sages, all those by whom this ancient lore has been heard worship the Supreme Self again and again.

sanskrit: idam ākhyānam ārṣeyaṃ pāraṃparyāgataṃ nṛpa nāvāsudevabhaktāya tvayā deyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: This tale, sprung from the seers and come down through the unbroken succession, O king, you must in no way give to one who is not a devotee of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: matto 'nyāni ca te rājann upākhyānaśatāni vai yāni śrutāni dharmyāṇi teṣāṃ sāro 'yam uddhṛtaḥ
english: And of the other hundreds of righteous narratives that you have heard from me, O king, this is the essence drawn forth.

sanskrit: surāsurair yathā rājan nirmathyāmṛtam uddhṛtam evam etat purā vipraiḥ kathāmṛtam ihoddhṛtam
english: As the nectar of immortality was churned and drawn forth of old by gods and demons, O king, so this nectar of discourse was here drawn forth by the brahmins.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ yaś cedaṃ śṛṇuyān naraḥ ekāntabhāvopagata ekānte susamāhitaḥ
english: And the man who recites this constantly, and who listens to this, having come to single-minded devotion, well composed in solitude —

sanskrit: prāpya śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ bhūtvā candraprabho naraḥ sa sahasrārciṣaṃ devaṃ praviśen nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: — that man, having reached the great White Island and become radiant as the moon, shall enter into the god of a thousand rays; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: mucyed ārtas tathā rogāc chrutvemām āditaḥ kathām jijñāsur labhate kāmān bhakto bhaktagatiṃ vrajet
english: The afflicted one would be freed from his sickness by hearing this tale from the beginning; the seeker after knowledge gains his desires, and the devotee attains the goal of the devotees.

sanskrit: tvayāpi satataṃ rājann abhyarcyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ sa hi mātā pitā caiva kṛtsnasya jagato guruḥ
english: By you too, O king, the Supreme Person is ever to be worshipped; for he is the mother and the father, and the teacher of the entire world.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyadevo bhagavān prīyatāṃ te sanātanaḥ yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho mahābāhur janārdanaḥ
english: May the blessed, eternal god, friend of the brahmins, be gracious to you — the mighty-armed Janārdana, O mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira.
